blocks.title: Grinding takes the stump. **What comes next fixes the yard.**
body: HD Landscape grinds stumps in St. Clair Shores and across Metro Detroit. A stump grinder is a machine with a toothed wheel that chews the stump into wood chips, down below the level of the lawn. Iowa State University Extension calls it the quickest, easiest and safest way to remove a stump.

The catch is what it leaves behind: a pile of wood shavings in the hole. Left there, shavings make it hard for new grass or plants to grow. So the plan covers what happens to the spot. Tell us what you want there next and we will set it up for that.

blocks.title: From stump to a spot you can use.

steps.title: Look
steps.body: Jake looks at the stump and what is around it, or starts from a photo. Tell him what you want in that spot next, because it changes the plan.

steps.title: Mark
steps.body: Buried lines get marked before digging. Michigan requires a notice to MISS DIG 811 at least three business days ahead.

steps.title: Grind
steps.body: The stump comes down below grade, along with any big roots at the surface that are in the way.

steps.title: Reset
steps.body: Shavings come out where they need to, topsoil goes in a little high for settling, and the spot is ready for sod, a bed or stone.

blocks.footnote: Locators mark public utility lines, not private ones like sprinkler systems, invisible dog fences or a feed to a shed or detached garage. A private locating company can mark those for a fee. If you have any near the stump, tell us where they run.

blocks.title: What goes where the stump was.
blocks.intro: A ground stump leaves soil full of wood, and wood changes how that soil holds water and feeds plants. Here is what to do about it, depending on what comes next.

items.title: Lawn
items.body: Get the shavings out, add topsoil a little above grade and let it settle, then lay sod or seed. Iowa State University Extension says buried wood ties up nitrogen and dries out fast, which is why grass struggles there. [We lay sod](/sod-installation/).

items.title: A new bed
items.body: A stump in the middle of the yard is a good excuse for a bed. With the shavings out and fresh soil in, the spot is ready for [new planting](/plant-installation/) or [rock and stone](/rock-and-stone-installation/).

items.title: A new tree
items.body: Not in the same hole. Iowa State University Extension advises planting at least three feet away, ideally six to eight, because old roots and sawdust get in the way. If the old tree died of a disease or pest, choose a tree that problem does not affect.

blocks.title: In a fenced yard, **the gate matters.**
body: St. Clair Shores is home base for HD Landscape, and it is a tightly built city. General one family zoning here allows lots as small as 6,000 square feet, so getting a grinder to a backyard stump is a real question here. Before we quote it, we want to know how the machine gets in.
The easiest way to start is a text with two photos: the stump and the narrowest spot on the way to it. Here is what helps Jake give you a straight answer.

blocks.title: On time, itemized and left clean.

faq.q: Do you do stump grinding in St. Clair Shores?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape grinds stumps in St. Clair Shores, where the business is based, and across Metro Detroit. Lots are tight in much of this town, so start with two photos: the stump and the narrowest gate on the way to it.

faq.q: How much does stump grinding cost?
faq.a: The size of the stump sets most of it, along with how the grinder gets in and what sits close by. A clear photo is enough to get started, and a free itemized estimate comes from there.

faq.q: How deep do you grind a stump?
faq.a: Below grade, so lawn or a new bed can go back on top. Iowa State University Extension puts a typical grind at 8 to 12 inches. If you plan to plant in that spot, tell us before we start.

faq.q: What happens to the wood chips after stump grinding?
faq.a: Grinding leaves a big pile of shavings. If the spot is going back to lawn or a bed, most of that should come out, because wood in the soil makes it hard for new plants to grow. We will go over the plan for the shavings with you and put it on the estimate.

faq.q: Can grass grow where a stump was ground?
faq.a: Yes, once the spot is prepared. The wood shavings should come out, topsoil goes in slightly above grade to allow for settling, and then sod or seed can go down. We can handle the [sod installation](/sod-installation/) as well.

faq.q: Can I plant a new tree in the same spot as the old stump?
faq.a: It is not ideal. Iowa State University Extension recommends planting at least three feet from the old spot, and ideally six to eight, because old roots and sawdust get in the way. If it has to be the same spot, waiting a year or two helps.

faq.q: Will a tree grow back after stump grinding?
faq.a: Some trees do send up sprouts after they are cut down. Tell Jake what kind of tree it was so he can tell you what to expect. If sprouts show up later, cut them off at the ground as they appear.

faq.q: Do you have to call MISS DIG before grinding a stump?
faq.a: Michigan requires a notice to MISS DIG 811 at least three business days before a digging project of any size or depth, and it is the responsibility of whoever does the work. The service is free. Private lines, like sprinkler systems, are not marked, so tell us if you have any nearby.

faq.q: Can you get a stump grinder into a fenced backyard?
faq.a: Often, but it depends on the gate and the path to the stump. Text a photo of the stump and the narrowest gap on the way to it, and Jake can size up what it will take.

faq.q: Can you grind a stump left from an old tree removal?
faq.a: Yes. The stump does not have to be from a tree we took down. Old stumps left behind by another company or a past owner are fine. If the tree is still standing and it is a smaller one, we can [take that down](/tree-trimming-and-removal/) too. A big one needs a tree company first, and we can grind what it leaves.

faq.q: Can I just leave the stump, or burn it out?
faq.a: You can leave it if it is out of the way, but it can take 10 years or more to rot on its own. Do not burn it. Iowa State University Extension warns that stump fires can burn for days and are hard to put out, and many cities do not allow them.

faq.q: How long does stump grinding take?
faq.a: The grinding itself is a matter of hours, and many stumps are finished in one visit, depending on size and access. Soil, sod or planting afterward can add time, and your estimate will show what is included.
